admission.justification: Two registered cases pin the remedies and the modifier-by-name reading. A false remedy costs the curator the whole refused batch and sends it to a route that cannot work, which is the failure the leaf removes.

applicability: The refusal a name-based proof meets for a JavaScript or TypeScript test case, and the remedy that refusal offers.
conditions: A .skipIf or .runIf case is reported with that modifier, not as .skip.
A case that runs and that no name reaches is offered its exact line_range.
A case that does not run is offered no line range.
exclusions: A symbol refusal in a language the extractor does not parse, which cites a line range or the file instead.
statement: A proof's refusal names the real modifier or the real title form, and offers a line_range only where a range reaches the case, so an author is never told to use a route that cannot work.
